Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis. Wet, cool weather favors its development.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply fungicides such as captan or myclobutanil. Prune trees to improve air circulation.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.

Apple___Black_rot.causes: Fungal infection by Botryosphaeria obtusa, spreads through wounds and dead wood.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Remove and destroy infected fruit and cankers. Apply appropriate fungicides.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Keep trees healthy and wound-free. Prune out dead wood regularly.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.causes: Fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae requiring both apple and cedar trees.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply fungicides during spring when spores are active.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby eastern red cedar trees. Plant resistant apple varieties.

Apple___healthy.causes: The plant is healthy and showing no signs of disease.
Apple___healthy.treatment: Continue standard care: proper watering, sunlight, and nutrition.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular monitoring and good garden hygiene.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.causes: Fungus Podosphaera clandestina, favored by high humidity and moderate temperatures.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate fungicides. Thin out branches for airflow.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant in full sun. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.causes: Fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis, favored by warm, humid conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply foliar fungicides. Harvest early if infection is severe.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate with non-host crops and till under infected debris.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.causes: Fungus Puccinia sorghi, spores spread by wind over long distances.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Fungicides are usually not needed unless infection is very early and severe.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids. Maintain proper plant spacing.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Fungus Exserohilum turcicum, favored by moderate temperatures and high humidity.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Fungicides can be effective if applied early in infection.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids. Rotate with non-host crops. Till under debris.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.causes: The plant is healthy and showing no signs of disease.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.treatment: Continue standard care: proper watering, sunlight, and nutrition.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular monitoring and good garden hygiene.

Grape___Black_rot.causes: Fungus Guignardia bidwellii, overwinters in mummified berries.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply fungicides like captan or mancozeb, especially before and after bloom.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified berries. Prune for good airflow. Remove infected debris.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).causes: Complex of fungi including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, enters through pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No curative treatment. Prune out infected wood and apply wound dressings.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid pruning during rain. Delay pruning until late winter.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.causes: Fungus Pseudocercospora vitis. Spreads in warm, moist conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides. Prune lower leaves to improve airflow.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Maintain vineyard floor hygiene. Prune vines properly.

Grape___healthy.causes: The plant is healthy and showing no signs of disease.

Grape___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular monitoring and good garden hygiene.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).causes: Bacteria Candidatus Liberibacter, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid pest.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure. Promptly remove and destroy infected trees to prevent spread.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Control the psyllid population. Use certified disease-free nursery stock.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacteria Xanthomonas campestris pv. pruni, overwinters in branch cankers.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based sprays during the dormant season.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant peach cultivars. Avoid late-summer nitrogen fertilization.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacteria Xanthomonas, spreads by water splash and contaminated seeds.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Use copper fungicides as a preventative. Remove infected debris.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use clean seeds. Maintain 3-year crop rotation. Avoid overhead watering.

Potato___Early_blight.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, favored by warm temperatures and high humidity.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Remove infected leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops. Ensure adequate nutrition. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Potato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans, a very aggressive pathogen.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Fungicides are essential. Destroy infected plants immediately to prevent spread.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed potatoes. Eliminate cull piles.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.causes: Fungi in the Erysiphaceae family, favored by high humidity (but not rain).
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply neem oil or sulfur-based fungicides. Increase plant spacing.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant in full sun. Choose resistant varieties.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.causes: Fungus Diplocarpon earliana. It overwinters in fallen leaves and spreads by water splash.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Apply fungicides (captan or copper). Remove and burn infected leaves.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Ensure good air circulation and drainage.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacteria Xanthomonas campestris, spreads via water splash and contaminated seeds.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Copper-based sprays may suppress the disease. Remove infected plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use pathogen-free seed. Rotate crops. Avoid working in wet fields.

Tomato___Early_blight.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, favored by warm humid conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Use copper-based fungicides. Trim lower leaves to improve airflow.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch to prevent soil splash. Stake plants. Practice crop rotation.

Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Phytophthora infestans, spreads rapidly in cool wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply fungicides preventatively. Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead watering. Plant resistant varieties. Space plants properly.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.causes: Fungus Passalora fulva, primarily affects greenhouse tomatoes in high humidity.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Apply sulfur or copper fungicides. Reduce humidity using ventilation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Prune for airflow. Avoid wetting leaves. Choose resistant hybrids.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.causes: Fungus Septoria lycopersici, one of the most common tomato diseases.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves. Apply chlorothalonil or copper-based fungicides.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops. Mulch plants. Do not handle plants when wet.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.causes: Small pests (Tetranychus urticae) that suck plant fluids, favored by hot dry weather.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Spray with insecticidal soap or neem oil. Release predatory mites.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Keep plants well-watered. Hose down plants frequently to wash off mites.

Tomato___Target_Spot.causes: Fungus Corynespora cassiicola, spreads during warm and wet periods.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Apply fungicides (azoxystrobin or mancozeb). Improve air circulation.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Increase row spacing. Avoid overhead irrigation. Remove old plant debris.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.causes: Virus spread by the silverleaf whitefly pest.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No cure. Remove infected plants. Focus on whitefly management.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use insect netting. Plant resistant cultivars. Destroy weeds.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.causes: Viral infection (ToMV) spread by contact, seeds, or pests like aphids.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: There is no cure for the virus. Remove infected plants immediately.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use virus-free seeds. Wash hands/tools often. Control aphid populations.

Tomato___healthy.treatment: Continue standard care: proper watering, sunlight, and nutrition.
